p: Look at the map. Which section is on the left of the Auditorium?
ex: Left is your left hand's side of the map. A section is left of the Auditorium.

p: The B section is on the ___ of the Auditorium.
ex: B section is on your right hand's side of the Auditorium: right.

p: What is between the A section and the B section?
ex: The Auditorium has A on one side and B on the other: it is between.

p: Where is the Auditorium?
o: between the A and B sections
ex: The A section and the B section are on its sides, so it is between them.

p: Where is Gym/Court 1 on the map?
o: at the top, on the right
at the top, on the left
at the bottom, on the right
ex: Gym/Court 1 is at the top of the map, on the right side.

p: Where is Gym/Court 2 on the map?
o: at the top, on the left
at the top, on the right
at the bottom, on the left
ex: Gym/Court 2 is at the top of the map, on the left side.

p: What is between Gym/Court 2 and Gym/Court 1?
ex: C section has a gym on each side, so it is between the two gyms.

p: Which two places are above the Patio?
ex: On this map, the Treehouse and the Trix are above the Patio.

p: Where is the Entrance?
ex: The Entrance is low on the map, under the Auditorium.

p: Which place is under everything on the map?
ex: The Drive is at the very bottom of the map, under everything.

p: Look at the map. Which place is on your right-hand side?
ex: Left and right are the sides of the person looking. Gym/Court 1 is on the right.

p: The Treehouse is on the ___ of the Trix.
ex: The Treehouse is on your left hand's side of the Trix: left.

p: The red pin marks a place on this map. Which place?
ex: A red pin marks a place. Here it marks a Year 2 classroom.

p: The red pin is near which section?
ex: The red pin is at the top of B section, so it is near B section.

p: What does a red pin do on a map?
ex: A red pin marks a place on the map.

p: What kind of map is this?
ex: It shows classrooms, gyms and the Auditorium, so it is a map of the school.

p: A blue line on the screen shows the way to go. What is it?
ex: A GPS route shows the way to go with a line on the map.

p: You want to see all of São Paulo. Which one do you need?
ex: São Paulo is a city, so we need a map of a city.

p: Which two are kinds of maps?
o: a city map and a GPS route
a red pin and a city map
a red pin and a GPS route
ex: City maps and GPS routes are maps. A red pin only marks a place.

p: When we read maps, we need to pay a lot of attention to…
ex: Map rule: pay a lot of attention to the details and the path.

p: On a map, the path is…
ex: Path means way: it is the way we are going.

p: We might get ___ if we run or don't pay attention.
ex: If we run or don't pay attention to the map, we might get lost.

p: Why might we get lost?
o: We run or don't pay attention.
We look at the map details.
We look at the path we take.
ex: We might get lost if we run or don't pay attention.

p: This tower is seen from the...
ex: From the front, you stand on the ground and look straight. This photo shows that.

p: This tower is seen from the...
ex: From the top, you look down and see the ground. This photo shows that.

p: This tower is seen from the...
ex: From the side, you see the whole tower and what is next to it.

p: This tower is seen from the...
ex: From the bottom, you look up and the tip is far away.

p: You stand under the tower and look up. You see it from the...
ex: Under the tower and looking up means the view from the bottom.

p: You go up the tower and look down. You see it from the...
ex: Up high and looking down means the view from the top.

p: You are on the grass. The tower is straight ahead of you. You see it from the...
ex: Straight ahead of you, looking straight: that is the view from the front.

p: You can see the whole tower and the river near it. You see it from the...
ex: The side view shows the whole tower and the river near it.

p: Complete: Our perspective changes depending on ___ we are looking from.
ex: Perspective changes depending on WHERE we look from: top, bottom, front or side.

p: Complete: We can see many things from different ___.
ex: We see things from different positions. Top, bottom, front and side are positions.

p: Ana looks at the tower from the top. Leo looks from the bottom. It is one tower. Why do they see different things?
o: They look at two different towers.
They look at it on different days.
ex: Perspective depends on where we look from. Ana and Leo are in different positions.

p: One object makes these three shadows. What shapes are they?
ex: One object, three shadows: a triangle, a rectangle and a circle.

p: What shape is the shadow on the floor?
ex: The floor shows the shadow from the bottom of the object: a circle.

p: What shape is the shadow on the left wall?
ex: The shadow on the left wall has three corners, so it is a triangle.

p: What shape is the shadow on the right wall?
ex: The shadow on the right wall has four corners, so it is a rectangle.

p: There is one object, but there are three different shadows. Why?
o: Each side of it is different.
ex: The same object makes different shadows from each side. Each side gives another shape.

p: Complete: People are not right or wrong. They just have a different ___ of things.
ex: The giraffe sentence says people just have a different view of things.

p: The giraffe's head is up high. The woman is down low. Why do they see things differently?
o: The giraffe is right about it.
The woman is right about it.
ex: Nobody is wrong here. They look from different positions, so they have different views.

p: Ana sees a triangle shadow. Leo sees a circle shadow. It is the same object. What can we say?
o: Ana is right, Leo is wrong.
Leo is right, Ana is wrong.
ex: People are not right or wrong. Ana and Leo just have different views.
